title: Fraunhofer’s X-ray system reveals the inner workings of battery cells - electrive.com
content:
The Fraunhofer EMI has developed a special X-ray technology that makes dynamic processes in large-format prismatic cells visible in real time. Together with Volkswagen's battery subsidiary PowerCo, this technology is now set for industrial application.
Such an X-ray system will be installed at the PowerCo site in Salzgitter in 2028.
Image: Fraunhofer EMI
The Fraunhofer Institute for High-Speed Dynamics, Ernst-Mach-Institut, describes its innovative X-ray technology as a ‘globally unique high-speed X-ray system’. According to scientists at the institute, it reveals what happens inside large-format battery cells in fractions of a second under stress – and could help accelerate the development of safer cell generations for the European automotive industry.
The approach aims to answer what occurs inside a battery cell when it fails. Until now, cell manufacturers and vehicle integrators have relied on simulations, destructive testing methods, or indirect measurements. However, the method developed by Fraunhofer EMI now enables a direct view into the operating cell. According to the team, the system combines high-performance X-ray technology with a specially developed battery test chamber and comprehensive sensor technology for the simultaneous recording of temperature, pressure, voltage, and gas flow: “Recording up to 1,000 images per second, it reveals processes such as gas formation, material displacement, and crack propagation inside the cell at extremely high resolution—events that until now have remained hidden from view.”
Dr Sebastian Schopferer, Head of Battery Safety at Fraunhofer EMI, emphasises: “Our in-situ method allows us to see what happens inside a cell in fractions of a second—in real time and at the highest resolution. This fundamentally changes how we understand battery design and safety.” A key engineering achievement was the development of a protective chamber that reliably shields sensitive X-ray components from the extreme conditions during the thermal runaway of lithium-ion cells.
The battery cell is placed into the X-ray system.
The relevance of this approach is further demonstrated by strong industry interest: Fraunhofer EMI explained it has already characterised material ejection during thermal runaway and propagation behaviour in multi-cell setups for several German car manufacturers, including VW and Audi. According to a statement: “The resulting data enables engineers to assess cell designs based on directly observed processes and refine simulation models with greater precision—delivering direct added value for product development and certification processes.”
The project is closely linked to PowerCo, Volkswagen’s battery subsidiary. During its next stage, Fraunhofer EMI and PowerCo aim to jointly transition the technology into industrial application. The institute contributes its expertise in materials research, battery abuse testing, and high-speed imaging, while PowerCo provides the requirements for series production and access to real cell types.
Initial results from the collaboration are already being incorporated into the development of optimised series cells at PowerCo. While this still involves logistical effort, there’s an end in sight: by 2028, a corresponding X-ray system is set to be installed at PowerCo’s site in Salzgitter. The system is scalable for various cell formats and new cell chemistries – “an important advantage for the development of future battery generations,” according to the Fraunhofer Institute.
Still image from an X-ray video during a nail penetration test of a prismatic lithium-ion cell.
HW Vassen, CTO at PowerCo, commented: “With in-situ high-speed X-ray imaging, we are taking battery research to a new level. For the first time, we can make the dynamic processes inside cells visible in real time and in slow motion. This unprecedented depth of insight allows us to optimize battery cell safety and design in a highly targeted way and bring innovations into industrial use much faster. Together with Fraunhofer EMI, we are advancing high technology made in Europe and are strengthening Europe’s role in the battery industry.”
PowerCo was founded by the Volkswagen Group in 2022 and is responsible for the development and production of the group’s battery cells. The company is based in Salzgitter and is currently building three cell factories with a combined capacity of up to 200 gigawatt-hours per year: in Salzgitter (Germany), Valencia (Spain), and St. Thomas (Canada).

title: GM and LGES ramp up cell production in Ohio again - electrive.com
content:
General Motors and LG Energy Solution are resuming battery cell production at their joint plant in Ohio, USA, after a pause of around seven months. Starting next week, cells for GM electric vehicles will be manufactured there again. The restart comes as the partners increasingly focus other US capacities on stationary battery storage systems.
Battery cell production for GM electric vehicles resumes at the Ultium Cells plant in Ohio.
Image: GM
Production at the Ultium Cells plant in north-eastern Ohio will resume next Monday – with most of the temporarily laid-off workers set to return to the site,
reports. In total, around 1,400 people are expected to work there again.
Cell production was halted in January 2026 due to declining demand for EVs. After a seven-month hiatus, the joint venture between GM and LG Energy Solution (LGES) will now restart manufacturing battery cells for the US carmaker’s electric vehicles. The restart comes as GM and LGES have aligned their North American battery capacities more closely with shifting demand. This adjustment is particularly evident at the second Ultium Cells plant in Spring Hill, Tennessee, where the partners are investing $70 million to retrofit production lines. The goal is to manufacture
LFP cells for stationary energy storage systems
in the future.
However, the conversion in Tennessee does not signal a complete shift away from EV batteries. Ultium Cells describes it as a diversification of the site, with plans to produce cells for both stationary storage systems and electric vehicles in the future. Spring Hill is part of a broader strategy: LG Energy Solution aims to offset weaker-than-expected demand for electric vehicles by expanding its energy storage business. The company plans to increase its global production capacity for energy storage systems to over 60 GWh by 2026, with more than 80 per cent of this capacity located in North America.
GM has also responded to weaker demand. At the beginning of the year, the group took
billion-dollar write-downs
related to its EV business. This was partly due to dampened demand expectations following the end of the US tax credit of $7,500 for new EVs in September 2025.
Meanwhile, GM is restructuring its other battery partnerships. According to
, Samsung SDI acquired GM’s stake in the joint venture for a
battery cell factory still under construction in the state of Indiana
earlier this week. The restart of production in Ohio highlights a different focus: there, GM and LGES are ramping up their EV battery capacities again after a seven-month pause, while Spring Hill demonstrates how the partners are simultaneously broadening their cell production strategy.

title: China's Tianneng warns of profit fall as lead battery material costs rise – Batteries International
content: Tianneng Power International has warned of a potential half-year profit fall of up to 66% as high raw material costs hit its mainstay lead acid battery business — but said long-term prospects are strong. The China-based lead battery major, part of the Tianneng Group, issued the profit warning on August 7, saying revenue for the six months ended last June is expected to be down by 5%-8% compared to the year ago period. Upstream raw material prices such as for sulfuric acid, which remain at relatively high levels, are to blame — along with intensified competition in downstream industries, Tianneng said in its Hong Kong stock exchange filing. Another contributory factor was the additional VAT deduction applicable to advanced manufacturing companies in mainland China. However, Tianneng said lead acid battery sales remained generally stable, thanks to the firm’s leading market position and solid customer base. Meanwhile, its Li ion battery business, synergies in battery recycling operations and expansion into overseas markets is proceeding steadily. Interim first-half results are expected to be published toward the end of this month. International expansion In terms of expansion, Tianneng has revealed it commissioned a manufacturing base in Indonesia last June. The company plans to establish a “full-lifecycle lead battery industry chain” in the country and expand into lithium motive power, energy storage systems, start-stop and industrial power batteries. Separately, Tianneng said it had signed a cooperation agreement with US lead and lithium giant Clarios last May, focusing on the raw material supply chain, waste battery recycling, and full lifecycle management. Tianneng said in 2018 was considering setting up a factory in another, unspecified Asian country, to produce 100,000 tonnes of lead batteries a year. title: GM Battery Strategy Shift: Samsung Exit, Ultium Restart
content:
Automotive & Mobility
Battery Manufacturing
The automaker's diverging battery partnerships reflect broader industry restructuring as Ford and Stellantis also recalibrate US battery manufacturing strategies.
August 13, 2026
5 Min Read
General Motors corporate logo shines from the Hudson's Detroit building Friday, October 10, 2025 after being affixed overnight to the company's future global headquarters in downtown Detroit, Michigan.
John F. Martin / General Motors
At a Glance
Samsung SDI acquires GM's stake in Indiana battery JV; facility to focus on energy storage systems instead of EV batteries
GM-LG Energy Solution's Ohio Ultium plant resumes production after 7-month shutdown, bringing back 1,400 workers
Ford and Stellantis also restructuring battery partnerships, reflecting industry-wide recalibration amid softer EV demand
General Motors is reshaping its North American battery manufacturing footprint through a pair of significant moves that signal both retreat and renewal in the automaker's electrification plans. The company has ended one joint venture while reviving another, reflecting broader industry adjustments to slower-than-expected electric vehicle demand and growing opportunities in stationary energy storage.
Samsung SDI takes full control of Indiana facility
On August 11, Samsung SDI announced
it had acquired GM's 49.99% stake in SynergyCells
, their $3.5 billion joint venture battery plant under construction in New Carlisle, IN. The ownership change effectively ends GM's participation in the project, which was originally announced in 2024 with plans to produce 27 gigawatt-hours of EV batteries annually.
"While reflecting recent market changes, this acquisition decision is to continue the strategic partnership with GM," a Samsung SDI official stated in the announcement. "We will continue our commitment to an electrified future with the partner, while utilizing the plant to proactively respond to the fast-growing ESS market in the U.S."
Related:
Ford Unveils Fathom Electric Pickup at $29,945 With Frunk & Bi-Directional Charging Capability
Samsung SDI President & CEO Yoon-ho Choi flanked by GM executives at the JV signing event in 2024. Credit: Samsung SDI
The decision reflects pressure on global automakers and battery makers to scale back or adjust investment plans, particularly following
the Trump administration's elimination of EV incentives
. The loss of the federal $7,500 consumer tax credit in September 2025 has weighed heavily on EV demand across the industry.
Despite the joint venture dissolution, Samsung SDI and GM signed a new agreement to jointly develop next-generation prismatic battery cells featuring high energy density and fast charging capability for potential future EV applications. Samsung SDI plans to initially use the Indiana facility for energy storage system battery production before potentially incorporating the co-developed prismatic cells.
Ohio Ultium Cells plant returns to operation
In contrast to the Indiana development, GM's partnership with LG Energy Solution is experiencing a revival. The Ultium Cells joint venture plant in Warren, OH
resumed battery cell production on August 18
after a seven-month shutdown, according to The Korea Herald.
The restart brings approximately 1,400 workers back to the facility, including most of the roughly 850 employees who were temporarily laid off when production halted in January 2026. The Ohio plant, Ultium Cells' first manufacturing facility, has an annual production capacity of approximately 35 gigawatt-hours and produces battery cells for GM electric vehicles.
Related:
Hyundai Ioniq 9 AWD Performance Calligraphy Delivers Strong Range & Fast Charging Capability
Tom Gallagher, Ultium Cells' vice president of operations,
confirmed the restart
to Reuters, as reported by CBT News. The resumption is expected to lift LG Energy Solution's overall plant utilization rate from 52.8% in the first half of 2026 to above 60% in the second half, according to The Korea Herald.
Tennessee facility pivots toward energy storage
While Ohio returns to EV battery production, GM and LG Energy Solution's second Ultium Cells plant in Spring Hill, Tennessee is undergoing a strategic transformation. According to Electrive, the partners are investing $70 million to retrofit production lines at the Tennessee facility to manufacture
lithium iron phosphate (LFP) cells for stationary energy storage systems
The Ultium Cells plant in Spring Hill, TN. Credit: GM
However, Ultium Cells characterizes this as a diversification rather than a complete pivot, with plans to produce cells for both stationary storage systems and electric vehicles at the site. This dual-purpose approach reflects LG Energy Solution's broader strategy to offset weaker EV demand by expanding its energy storage business. The company aims to increase its global production capacity for energy storage systems to over 60 gigawatt-hours by 2026, with more than 80% of this capacity located in North America.
Related:
Electric Aviation Progress with Hybrid and Fully Electric Systems
Broader industry restructuring of battery partnerships
GM's battery partnership recalibration reflects a wider pattern of restructuring across the US automotive industry. Ford Motor Company
dissolved its BlueOval SK battery joint venture with SK On
in December 2025, with the split completed in early 2026.. Ford took full ownership of two battery plants in Kentucky through a wholly owned subsidiary, while SK On assumed full control of the Tennessee plant at BlueOval City. The Kentucky plant
workforce faced layoffs beginning in February 2026
, with plans to rehire 2,100 employees in 2027 after retooling for energy storage system production, The Detroit News reported.
BlueOval SK battery plant in Kentucky. Credit: BlueOval SK
The dissolution was driven by diverging chemistry strategies
and Ford's pivot toward energy storage
). Ford is separately building a $3 billion wholly-owned LFP battery plant in Michigan using CATL technology through a licensing arrangement rather than a joint venture. The facility
began pilot production in mid-2026
, CBT News reported, and expects to produce launch-ready battery cells before the end of 2026, with an annual capacity of 35 gigawatt-hours—enough for 400,000 vehicles. This makes Ford the first automaker to produce LFP batteries in the US for mainstream EVs.
Stellantis has also been reconsidering its battery manufacturing strategy. Electrive reported in February 2026 that the company was exploring options
to exit its StarPlus Energy joint venture with Samsung SDI
, which is building two battery plants in Kokomo, IN. The first plant, with 33 gigawatt-hours of capacity, was expected to launch in the first quarter of 2025, while the second plant with 34 gigawatt-hours of capacity was
targeted to start production in 2027
, according to Samsung SDI.
Industry implications
The restructuring of battery joint ventures across GM, Ford, and Stellantis illustrates the complex calculus facing automakers and battery manufacturers in the current market environment. These partnerships, conceived during the EV boom of the early 2020s, are being reconfigured to accommodate market realities including reduced consumer demand and shifting chemistry preferences.
The pivot toward energy storage systems by Samsung SDI and LG Energy Solution reflects the rapid growth of the stationary storage market in the United States, driven by grid modernization needs and renewable energy integration. This diversification strategy allows battery manufacturers to leverage their North American production capacity across multiple applications rather than relying solely on automotive demand.
For the battery industry, these moves underscore the importance of manufacturing flexibility and the value of facilities capable of producing cells for multiple end markets and chemistries. As automakers continue to adjust their electrification timelines and production volumes, battery manufacturers are positioning themselves to serve both transportation and stationary storage applications from their US manufacturing bases, while also adapting to the industry's growing interest in LFP chemistry for cost-sensitive applications.

In today's world, supply chains are facing increasing levels of complexity, driven by a range of disruptive factors. With this complexity comes a range of solutions, aimed at increasing efficiency and cost savings.
These solutions, however, are not destined to work for each issue, and when used incorrectly, can be even more disruptive.
What does work is an increase of visibility, real-time data and a unity across supply chain operations. Supply chain orchestration helps coordinate and automate end-to-end supply chain processes, meaning a significant reduction in fragmentation and error.

Navigating turbulence
With supply chain complexity at an all-time high, siloed data flows can be catastrophic for organisations. From planning to final delivery,
visibility and collaboration
are critical for ensuring an optimised supply chain.
A synchronisation across inventory, transport and manufacturing helps businesses remain operable amid disruption, with automated co-ordination across and end-to-end supply chain.
As businesses look to automate their operations more, many are still failing to see the success of implementation. This failure is not caused by bad technological solutions, but by trying to use the wrong solution for a specific task. Increased
visibility and collaboration
helps avoid this, as leaders can gain full insights into their operations, which demonstrates where something needs supported.
In the growing age of digitalisation and agentic AI, supply chain orchestration is a valuable tool for helping leaders navigate ongoing geopolitical and market volatility.

RSPO 2026 Report Tracks Sustainable Palm Oil Supply Chains
Prioritise Us
on Google
Independent smallholder group can acquire an RSPO Certification, creating sustainable palm oil on local and global scales. Credit: RSPO
RSPO’s 2026 Impact Report tracks sustainable palm oil sourcing, with 20% of global production certified and manufacturers & retailers increasing compliance
Supply chain actors across manufacturing and retail are adopting certified sustainable
palm oil
at rates that could reshape tropical commodity flows.
According to the Roundtable on Sustainable Palm Oil (RSPO), 20% of global palm oil production now carries certification.
The RSPO 2026 Impact Report documents how voluntary standards are affecting procurement patterns and land management across producer regions.
Certified sustainable supply has expanded to protect more than 551,000 hectares of carbon-rich forests and high-conservation ecosystems.
RSPO Impact Update Video 2025
Certification networks expand across supply chains
The RSPO operates with approximately 6,300 voluntary members across three categories.
Ordinary members include organisations with direct supply chain involvement and associated NGOs, banks or investors.
Associate members purchase less than 500 tonnes of palm oil and
palm oil products
per year.
Affiliate members are organisations or individuals not directly involved in the palm oil supply chain.
According to the report, downstream actors show responsible sourcing target compliance past 56%.
Certified facilities have surpassed 7,500 globally and trademark licenses now span 94 countries.
This distribution could make tracing certified sustainable
palm oil
ingredients easier for manufacturers.
Downstream compliance rates rise
Under the RSPO Shared Responsibility framework, manufacturers and retailers are making progress on uptake targets.
Manufacturers show compliance rates of 61% and retailers have reached nearly 70% compliance.
These rates apply to actors purchasing certified sustainable palm oil through the RSPO system.
The framework requires downstream companies to set time-bound targets for certified material use.
Compliance is measured against these self-declared commitments.
More than 551,000 hectares of High Conservation Value, High Carbon Stock and vital peatland areas have been protected from land conversion under RSPO standards.
This area is nearly eight times the size of Singapore.
Joseph D'Cruz, CEO of RSPO. Credit: RSPO
"The data and information presented in this 2026 RSPO Impact Report make a compelling case: sustainable
palm oil
is working and the results are clearer than ever," says Joseph D'Cruz, CEO of RSPO, in the report.
Regulatory pressure affects sourcing decisions
Joseph notes that regulatory frameworks are raising requirements on deforestation, due diligence and supply chain transparency. Investors and fund managers are scrutinising environmental and social governance with greater rigour.
"Consumers are asking harder questions about the origins of the products they use," says Joseph.
"These shifts are not a threat to RSPO; rather, they validate the need for systems like ours that provide credible, transparent and well-governed impact."
Proactive monitoring has reduced environmental hazards in certified areas. According to the report, certified concessions account for only 1.38% of regional fire hotspots in Southeast Asia.
Mechanisms like the New Planting Procedure and zero-deforestation mandates are preserving biodiversity corridors. These protocols aim to stabilise ecosystem services while allowing production to continue.
Emissions reductions in processing operations
Climate accountability has become a focus for certified producers. Companies are quantifying and cutting GHG emissions across agricultural operations.
Through strict land-clearing protocols and improved Palm Oil Mill Effluent handling, certified operations avoid nearly 2.98m tonnes of CO₂e emissions annually. This is equivalent to removing almost 700,000 vehicles from the road.
Processing facilities are deploying methane capture technologies and solar installations. These measures reduce Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions while providing downstream partners with lower-carbon raw materials.
More than 660,000 direct workers operate within certified facilities protected by enforceable labour and human rights standards. The standards ensure fair compensation and safe working environments.

"The data proves that rigorous sustainability standards deliver verifiable impact on the ground," Yen Hun Sung, Director Standards and Sustainability at RSPO, tells Sustainability Magazine. "From forest conservation to economic workshops for women, RSPO Members are showing that sustainable palm oil production can actively safeguard ecosystems, mitigate climate change and uplift communities."
Smallholder integration through credit trading
Independent smallholder inclusion is advancing through direct credit trading models. According to the report, these models generated US$7.9m in direct financial benefits for smallholder groups in 2025 alone.
More than 17,000 smallholders have received targeted training programmes. The sector is fostering rural economies that align local agricultural livelihoods with global sustainability standards.
Smallholder integration allows independent producers to sell certified credits directly to buyers. This mechanism provides financial incentives for compliance with RSPO standards.
The training programmes cover farm management, certification requirements and safety protocols. Smallholder participation rates vary by region and producer network.
SD Guthrie Berhad's decarbonisation programme
SD Guthrie Berhad has established a net zero roadmap validated by the Science Based Targets initiative. The company aims for carbon neutrality across Scope 1 and 2 emissions by 2030 and net zero emissions by 2050.
The majority of emissions originate from POME. SD Guthrie is accelerating its renewables programme by deploying methane capture through 47 biogas plants across mill operations by 2030.
The company protects or restores more than 51,000 hectares of land. It has set aside 400 hectares of peat plantations in East Malaysia for restoration and is expanding reforestation efforts across non-productive areas.

"Through initiatives like our landscape-level sustainability partnership with WWF-Malaysia, we are working to move beyond simply reducing our footprint toward actively restoring the ecosystems we depend on," says Rashyid. Scope 3 engagement and labour remediation
Scope 3 emissions pose supply chain challenges for palm oil producers. SD Guthrie actively engages its value chain to ensure compliance.

Movianto is demonstrating its vaccine storage and distribution capabilities as the strategic logistics partner for NHS England with five year contract
NHS England
has activated a five-year pharmaceutical supply chain contract with Movianto UK following a competitive tender process.
The arrangement positions Movianto UK as the strategic logistics operator for national vaccination and immunisation programmes across England.
Infrastructure and storage network
The contract covers vaccine storage, inventory management, order fulfilment and GDP-compliant temperature-controlled distribution to more than 11,000 frontline healthcare locations.
Movianto UK, which became part of Yusen Logistics in 2025, operates healthcare distribution services across Europe.
Andy Robinson, Deputy Managing Director at Movianto UK, says, "The partnership brings together one of Europe's most advanced
healthcare logistics networks
with NHS England's national vaccination programmes, creating a more resilient, agile and efficient supply chain capable of supporting routine immunisation, national screening programmes and emergency public health responses."
Andy Robinson, Deputy Managing Director, Movianto UK
The infrastructure aims to support routine immunisation, national screening programmes and emergency public health responses.
The model replaces dedicated warehousing and transport infrastructure with access to Movianto UK's existing healthcare storage and
logistics network
. This network already serves pharmaceutical manufacturers, NHS organisations and UK Government departments.
This could deliver value through operational efficiency while maintaining regulatory compliance standards.
Direct supplier integration model
Suppliers can move product directly into Movianto's regulated storage network. This could reduce physical stock transfers between facilities before distribution to NHS providers.
Reduced transport movements could support Government and NHS sustainability targets to reduce carbon emissions across NHS procurement.
The contract draws on Movianto UK's work in national healthcare resilience. This spans pandemic preparedness, emergency response and time-critical delivery of
medicines and vaccines
across the UK.
MenB programme tests capacity
Movianto UK helped mobilise the national Meningococcal Group B vaccination programme for young people in July.
The company worked with NHS England and other national stakeholders to scale up operational capacity.
Vaccines reached community pharmacies and other providers on time. This followed reported meningococcal cases among university students in Kent.
The company says more than 16,000 orders have been processed and delivered.

National logistics infrastructure

This contract recognises the value of harnessing existing pharmaceutical infrastructure to create a smarter, more efficient operating model that benefits patients and the NHS alike.

healthcare delivery
while remaining ready to respond rapidly during national emergencies."
Neil Gibbons, Deputy Director of Performance and Delivery Improvement at NHS England, says: "The contract represents another significant milestone in NHS England's commitment to modernising national healthcare logistics through strategic partnerships that combine operational excellence, innovation, sustainability and value for money while strengthening resilience across the UK's healthcare supply chain.

title: Tesla defeats Sweden's IF Metall union after 1,021-day strike
content:
Fred Lambert
| Aug 13 2026 - 8:08 am PT
Sweden’s largest industrial union, IF Metall, is calling off its strike against Tesla after 1,021 days, the longest labor conflict in modern Swedish history. The union says it’s stopping because Tesla bought out every one of its striking members, leaving the walkout with nothing left to withhold.
The dispute started in October 2023 over a single demand: that Tesla sign a Swedish collective bargaining agreement for its mechanics. Nearly three years later, Tesla still hasn’t signed one. And now the union is standing down.
IF Metall announced today that it’s ending all conflict measures against Tesla effective 00:01 on August 19. In its statement, the union was blunt about why. Tesla “bought out” its members at the company, so the strike “no longer has any effect.”
The longest strike in modern Swedish history
The fight began on October 27, 2023, when Tesla’s roughly 120 mechanics across seven Swedish workshops walked off the job after Tesla refused to sign a kollektivavtal, the collective agreement that covers the vast majority of Swedish workplaces.
It snowballed fast as other unions started supporting Tesla workers. Dockworkers refused to unload Teslas at Swedish ports. Denmark, Norway, and Finland joined the port blockade. PostNord stopped delivering Tesla’s license plates. Electricians wouldn’t service Tesla’s chargers, and cleaners stopped cleaning its showrooms. We covered each escalation as it happened, from the
ports closing
to the fight reaching the Superchargers.
Tesla routed around all of it. It imported cars through Germany and trucked them up to Trelleborg, and it went to court to get plates directly rather than through the post. Elon Musk called the Swedish model “insane.” The company never budged.
How Tesla actually won
The union didn’t lose a vote or run out of money. Tesla simply paid its way out.
According to IF Metall, Tesla bought out all of its remaining striking members, one by one, until there was no one left on the picket line to represent. “Tesla has gigantic economic resources and has used them, among other things, to buy out the strikers. That is unique,” LO agreement secretary Veli-Pekka Säikkälä told Swedish outlet Ny Teknik.
IF Metall’s leadership framed it as a moral stand that ran into a wall of cash. “Our members at Tesla are union heroes who have fought for collective agreements against an employer with such a strong anti-union stance,” chair Marie Nilsson said, adding that three years of striking meant “enormous personal sacrifice.”
Contract secretary Simon Petersson went further, saying Tesla “is so opposed to collective agreements that they would rather buy out union members than offer secure conditions.” The union called it strikebreaking of a kind Sweden hasn’t seen in decades.
The sales never cracked — until Musk did
Here’s the part the union’s opponents will point to: the strike never actually hurt Tesla’s business in Sweden.
The Model Y was Sweden’s single best-selling car, of any kind, in both 2023 and 2024, straight through the blockade. Tesla registered 21,894 vehicles in Sweden in 2024, its best year in the country, with the strike in full swing. As
we reported in October 2024
, Tesla stayed dominant while the union fight dragged on with no visible effect on demand.
What finally broke Tesla’s Swedish sales wasn’t the union. It was Musk.
Registrations collapsed to 7,252 in 2025, down roughly 67% from 2024, as
Tesla’s sales cratered across Sweden
and the rest of Europe. That drop tracked the political backlash to Musk’s activities, not the labor dispute, which by then was old news. Sweden’s own registration data shows Tesla down 63% year-over-year through the first seven months of 2025.
2026 has been a partial recovery off that low base: 512 registrations in January, 553 in February, a 1,784-unit surge in March, then 429 in April and 858 in May. Better than 2025, still well below the pre-Musk-backlash peak.
So the union’s leverage argument was always shaky. It couldn’t dent Tesla’s sales at their height, and by the time sales did fall, a bigger force was doing the work.
Electrek’s Take
This is a clean loss for IF Metall.
The union picked a fight on principle, that Tesla should follow the Swedish model like everyone else, and Tesla answered with a checkbook. Buying out strikers one at a time until the bargaining unit is empty is ruthless, and it’s exactly the kind of thing the collective agreement system exists to prevent. If it holds up, it’s a template every foreign employer in Sweden just watched work.
But the sales data undercuts the union’s whole theory of the case. The strike was supposed to make Tesla feel enough pain to sign. It never did. The Model Y was Sweden’s top seller during the worst of the blockade, and the eventual collapse in 2025 came from Musk’s politics, not from dockworkers refusing to unload cars. Tesla proved a determined company can wait out even the most coordinated labor action in a country built around labor, as long as it’s willing to spend and absorb the bad press.
The bigger question now is whether this emboldens Tesla to take the same posture in Germany, where IG Metall has been circling Grünheide for years.

title: Volkswagen's new electric camper van turns the ID. Buzz into a home on wheels
content:
Volkswagen
VW ID BUZZ
ID. Buzz
Peter Johnson
| Aug 13 2026 - 7:33 am PT
Volkswagen
is giving people what they want — an all-electric, fully fledged camper van that can be assembled in minutes. The ID. California Cruise is coming as the first all-electric California camper.
Volkswagen reveals first electric California camper van
Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Stuff Bubble, which developed the world’s first inflatable camping kitchen, have teamed up to develop a new family of electric camper vans.
“This partnership gives us the opportunity to rethink the campervan,” Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles CEO, Stefan Mecha, said.
At Caravan Salon 2026 later this month, Volkswagen will unveil two new camper van concepts: the ID. California Cruise, the first fully electric member of the California family, and the California Beach, which the company says will unlock “maximum freedom.”
Volkswagen and Stuff Bubble are developing new inflatable camping equipment, or modules, that are lighter and easier to install.
According to VW, the special parts turn an everyday van into a “fully-fledged camper in just a few minutes,” without adding unnecessary weight or permanent fixtures.
The solution is perfect for those who “still want to enjoy the comforts of camping on spontaneous getaways, festival weekends, or outdoor adventures,” the company said. Unlike traditional camper van conversions, the parts can be installed by one person and removed just as quickly.
The inflatable kitchen was specifically designed to fit in the luggage shelf of the California Beach, with “full kitchen functionality,” despite weighing less than 23 lbs (10 kg). It even includes a closed water system.
The new inflatable bed is just as flexible, weighing just 12 lbs (6 kg) as a single or 26 lbs (12 kg) as a double.
Even with the bed installed, there’s plenty of room in the camper to cook, move around, or store things. The concept shown has enough room for four people to sleep.
At Caravan Salon, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles will reveal the ID. California Cruise for the first time. While the company didn’t share any other details, it did say the electric camper van will be based on the ID. Buzz.
Like the ID. Buzz, the ID. California Cruise will likely be available with 79- or 86-kWh battery pack options, which provide WLTP ranges of around 250-300 miles, depending on the trim.
The ID. California Cruise “marks an important milestone towards an entirely new generation of all-electric campervans,” Volkswagen said, set to arrive through 2028.
Volkswagen will reveal full details during Caravan Salon, which runs from August 28 to September 6. Check back for more.
Will Volkswagen bring the electric van to the US? It has yet to be confirmed, but Volkswagen doesn’t sell the current
California camper van
in the US.
The ID. Buzz is back on sale. After a brief hiatus, Volkswagen launched
the 2027 ID. Buzz
with a new Tourer model (pictured above) that essentially turns it into a camper van with a fold-out mattress and Overnight Mode. So, it wouldn’t be a surprise to see the ID. California Cruise go on sale in some form in the US as well.

title: Urban Arrow enters the longtail cargo e-bike market in US with its new Breeze
content:
Micah Toll
| Aug 13 2026 - 7:02 am PT
Urban Arrow has spent the last 14 years building a reputation around front-loading cargo bikes, becoming one of the biggest names in the family cargo bike world. Now the Dutch company is branching out into an entirely new category with the launch of the Urban Arrow Breeze, bringing its first-ever longtail electric cargo bike to the North American market.
While Urban Arrow’s signature
front box bikes
have long been popular with parents hauling kids and groceries, longtail cargo bikes have become an increasingly important part of the North American market. They offer much of the utility of a cargo bike while riding and feeling more like a conventional bicycle, making them an easier transition for riders who may be intimidated by larger front-loaders.
That’s exactly the audience Urban Arrow is targeting with the Breeze.
According to Urban Arrow North America General Manager Mark Danhof, longtail cargo bikes now make up the majority of the North American cargo bike segment, making this a natural expansion for the company.
The Breeze is built around 24-inch wheels instead of the more common 20-inch rear wheel seen on many longtails. Urban Arrow says the larger wheels create handling that feels closer to a standard bicycle while also improving stability at higher speeds and when carrying passengers.
Power comes from Bosch’s Cargo Line motor, paired with an Enviolo continuously variable hub transmission and Gates carbon belt drive. That’s a premium drivetrain combination that should appeal to riders looking for low maintenance and smooth operation.
Despite its relatively compact appearance, the Breeze is designed to haul some serious weight. The rear rack is rated to carry up to 176 lb (80 kg), enough for two children or a combination of passengers and cargo, while total payload capacity reaches 440 lb (200 kg). A very low step-through frame should also make mounting and dismounting easier, particularly when the bike is fully loaded.
Urban Arrow has also added several family-focused touches, including spoke and belt guards, a sturdy dual-leg kickstand for easier loading, Bosch’s Purion 200 display, integrated security features, and the MIK HD accessory mounting system on both the front and rear racks for quickly swapping between passenger and cargo setups.
The company is sweetening the launch with more than $700 worth of included accessories, including a passenger protection bar, footrests, seat cushions, and a front rack.
The Urban Arrow Breeze is available now through select dealers in the US and Canada in a single green colorway.
Pricing starts at $6,999
, putting it squarely in the premium cargo bike category, though the included accessories help soften the blow compared to many competitors that charge extra for those essentials.
Electrek’s Take
Urban Arrow already knows how to build excellent family cargo bikes, so it isn’t surprising to see the company bringing that expertise into the longtail segment. If anything, it’s surprising it took this long.
The longtail cargo bike design also makes a lot of sense for North America, as this style has become the default recommendation for many families looking to replace car trips because they offer a gentler learning curve than front-loaders while still carrying one or two kids with ease.
We shouldn’t really be surprised at the price, since Urban Arrow has long been a premium brand, so you’re going to have to pay to play when it comes to a Dutch cargo e-bike brand. At nearly $7,000 it certainly isn’t inexpensive, but neither is the rest of the premium cargo bike market. For families planning to rack up thousands of miles replacing school drop-offs and grocery runs, that investment may be easier to justify than it first appears.
I’m a bit surprised they only brought one colorway to the US, and not the darker option that debuted
when they launched this model in their home market of Europe last year
, but I guess they have their reasons.

title: Rivian's 2027 R1S adds captain's chairs, its most-requested feature
content:
Rivian R1T
Rivian R1S
Fred Lambert
| Aug 13 2026 - 7:00 am PT
The 2027 Rivian R1S's new second-row captain's chairs.
Rivian is rolling out its 2027 model year R1S and R1T, and the headline change is one owners have been asking for since day one: second-row captain’s chairs on the R1S.
The automaker calls it the single most-requested feature since the R1S launched. It arrives alongside a simplified trim structure, a new standard wheel for the R1T, a new paint color, and higher starting prices across the board.
Captain’s chairs finally come to the R1S
Until now, the R1S only came with a second-row bench. For MY2027, Rivian is adding a six-seat layout built around a center pass-through, so passengers can walk back to the third row without folding a seat or disturbing a child seat mounted in the second row.
The new six-seat configuration is built around a center pass-through.
Each captain’s chair gets an individual armrest that stows flush into the seat and a push-to-release cup holder that folds down from the inside edge. Both seats are heated, fold flat, and keep the full car-seat tie-downs from the bench setup. Skis and other long gear can slide down the middle while all six seats stay occupied.
If you’d rather keep three seats in the middle, the seven-seat bench sticks around. It’s standard on R1S Premium and on the Black Mountain Signature interior for Performance and Quad.
The catch is the price. On Premium trim, the captain’s chairs require the Sound + Vision package, so the option runs $4,000 with the Black Mountain interior and $6,000 with Ocean Coast. On Performance and Quad, the chairs start at $1,500 with Black Mountain Signature, and two interiors, Ocean Coast Signature and Slate Sky Signature, are only available if you check the captain’s chairs box, at $4,000 and $4,500 respectively.

The Dual/Tri/Quad names are gone
Rivian is also killing the motor-count naming that defined the R1 lineup. Out go Dual, Tri, and Quad as battery-and-motor combos; in come three trim tiers: Premium, Performance, and Quad. It mirrors the structure Rivian
rolled out on the R2
, so the two families now read the same way.
Premium is the dual-motor tier, with 533 horsepower and 610 lb-ft of torque, and a 0-60 mph time of 4.5 seconds. An optional power upgrade pushes it to 665 hp and a 3.4-second sprint, and a Long Range pack is rated at up to 410 miles on the R1S and 420 miles on the R1T.
Performance is the tri-motor tier at 850 hp and 1,103 lb-ft, good for 2.9 seconds to 60 and up to 371 miles of range. Quad stays the
halo of the lineup
with 1,025 hp, 1,198 lb-ft, a 2.5-second 0-60 on the R1T, and up to 374 miles.
Interior names change too. Performance and Quad get three Signature interiors: Slate Sky Signature, Black Mountain Signature, and Ocean Coast Signature. Premium offers Black Mountain and Ocean Coast.
A new trail wheel and a new color
The R1T picks up a new standard 20-inch Adventure All-Season wheel and Goodyear tire, meant to add off-road traction without the usual range hit from a more aggressive tire. It’s standard on R1T Premium and a no-cost option on R1T Performance, and Rivian rates it at 300 miles on Premium, 380 miles on Premium Long Range, and 348 miles on Performance.
Both trucks also get Esker Silver, the liquid-metal finish Rivian first showed on the R2. It replaces LA Silver as the included paint on the R1S and R1T.
The new Esker Silver finish on the 2027 Rivian R1T.
Esker Silver replaces LA Silver as the included R1 paint.
Esker Silver first appeared on the Rivian R2.
The 2027 Rivian R1S in Esker Silver.
The R1T’s new standard 20-inch Adventure All-Season wheel.
Prices are up
The MY2027 R1S now starts at $83,990 and the R1T at $79,990. That’s a jump from the
2026 model year
, where the R1S opened at $76,990 and the R1T at $70,990. The cheapest way into an R1 went up $7,000 on the SUV and $9,000 on the truck.
Electrek’s Take
The captain’s chairs are significant, and overdue, add-on that might bring some demand back to the R1S amid a focus on R2. A three-row family SUV without a walk-through middle row was always an odd gap in the R1S, especially at $80,000-plus, and Rivian is right to call it the most-requested feature. Building it around a center pass-through that doesn’t force you to disturb a car seat is exactly the kind of detail Rivian tends to get right.
The trim simplification is smart too. “How many motors do you want?” was never a great way to sell a car to a normal buyer, and lining the R1 up with the R2 gives the whole brand one language. I like it.
But the price is the part buyers will actually feel. A $7,000-to-$9,000 bump on the entry point, plus captain’s chairs that can cost $4,500 once you’re forced into the Sound + Vision package on Premium, adds up fast. Rivian is leaning harder into premium positioning right as the
more affordable R2
gets close to launch. That’s probably the plan: push R1 up-market and let R2 catch the volume. The question is how many R1S shoppers were waiting on captain’s chairs at the old price, not this one.

title: Ford's EV pickup is almost here, promising much more than an affordable price tag
content:
Peter Johnson
| Aug 13 2026 - 6:00 am PT
The Ford Fathom will go on sale in early 2027, starting at $28,350.
said the electric pickup is on track to go into production at its Louisville Assembly plant in Q1 2027.
Ford Fathom EV pickup enters production in Q1 2027
revealed the name and starting price
of the upcoming midsize electric pickup last week, the first vehicle based on its Universal EV (UEV) platform.
The first prototypes will roll off the assembly lines at Ford’s 3-million-square-foot Louisville Assembly Plant (LAP) in the first quarter of 2027.
announced plans
a year ago to transform it from a gas-powered vehicle plant into a facility for building fully electric vehicles, starting with the Fathom.
The $5 billion investment will create 4,000 new jobs at both the Louisville Assembly Plant and BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, and it will help fund the new equipment needed for the UEV platform. That’s where things get interesting.
The assembly process is a step change from Ford’s and most traditional automakers’ current manufacturing methods. Instead of a fully assembled vehicle rolling down the line, the UEV Production System breaks the vehicle into three sections: the front clip, rear clip, and battery deck.
Covered Ford Fathom UEV Production System at the Louisville Assembly Plant (Source: Ford)
Ford will use large unicastings to build the front and rear body sections. The single large aluminum casting piece replaces dozens of stamped and other welded components it currently uses.
The method cuts the number of parts from 146 to build the current Maverick to just two for the Fathom.
In the third line, the interior components (seats, consoles, and carpeting) are installed on top of the battery housing, which serves as the vehicle’s floor. The battery itself is then attached from the bottom.
Ford Fathom prototype (Source: Screenshot/ Ford)
Ford said the UEV Production System will enable it to assemble the Fathom 40% faster than current vehicles at the plant.
It’s also more ergonomic, Bryce Currie, Ford’s chief manufacturing officer, said, which will “require less twisting, turning, and bending.”
“We’ve engineered an 84% reduction in reaching over the fender,” Currie explained, adding, “The wiring harness is also more than 4,000 feet shorter and 22 pounds lighter than in our first-gen
electric SUV, making it much easier to install.”
(Source: Ford)
Ford is reinvesting some of the time it saves during assembly into insourcing and automation to improve quality and cost. LAP will have the highest level of automation in final assembly across all Ford plants globally.
For example, Ford installed a software module flash station, a first at one of its assembly plants, to ensure the vehicle has the latest software before the vehicle is fully built.
Before, if an issue were detected, updates would take about 10 minutes per vehicle. Now, it can be done as the vehicle rolls down the assembly line. With 5G in the facility, operators can diagnose and perform quality checks instantly.
Ford Universal EV Production System (Source: Ford)
With fewer parts and steps in the process, there’s less opportunity for issues to arise, Ford said, which will help improve quality.
The new UEV Production System and assembly tree will go online in the first quarter of 2027, starting with the Ford Fathom.
Ford said the Fathom will have more interior passenger space than a Toyota RAV4. It will also be equipped with a large, high-resolution touchscreen, bidirectional charging enabling vehicle-to-load (V2L) capabilities, a digital key, and Apple CarPlay and Android Auto as standard.
The Ford Fathom will also be the first vehicle to have

title: Rivian's long-delayed ALSO e-bike is only delayed a little bit longer
content:
Micah Toll
| Aug 13 2026 - 4:28 am PT
The wait for Rivian’s first electric bike just got a little bit shorter. After months of delays, ALSO has informed reservation holders that they’ll finally be able to place pre-orders for the company’s highly anticipated TM-B electric bike starting August 18.
It’s welcome news for the unknown number of people who put down reservations, though it’s hard to ignore just how far the timeline has slipped.
When ALSO first unveiled the TM-B
last year
, the company targeted Spring 2026 deliveries. Spring has now come and gone, and with Summer well upon us now, reservation holders are only now getting the opportunity to actually order their bikes – or at least they’re being told that such an opportunity will be coming very soon.
No customer TM-B bikes have been reported as delivered yet, meaning the first shipments are still ahead of us.
The latest email from ALSO explains that the company’s Gear Shop pre-order opening was itself pushed back by another week, from August 11 to August 18, so the company could align Gear Shop purchases with bike ordering for “the best and most seamless experience.”
One point of frustration that’s been bubbling up in the reservation community is ALSO’s decision to open ordering for all reservation holders at once.
Rather than giving earlier reservation holders priority based on when they put down their deposits, everyone appears to be entering the ordering process simultaneously.
For customers who reserved last year, that’s understandably rubbed some people the wrong way, especially since ALSO’s reservation page still includes language indicating that reservation order impacts fulfillment, stating that “The sooner you reserve, the sooner you ride” and “Reservations will be fulfilled on a first-come basis.”
The TM-B itself remains one of the more technically ambitious e-bikes we’ve seen in years. The lightweight urban bike features Rivian-inspired industrial design, a carbon belt drive, integrated lighting, a removable battery, connected features, GPS tracking, automatic electronic shifting, pedal-by-wire, and a suite of sensors intended to improve security and the riding experience. It was designed to be more of a premium mobility platform than just another commuter e-bike.
The catch, of course, is
the price
. The bike is priced at US $4,500 for the Performance version or $3,500 for the lower-range version with a smaller battery.
The TM-B enters an increasingly competitive market
at a time when many buyers are gravitating toward value-oriented e-bikes that deliver much but not all of the performance of a TMB, yet for a fraction of the cost. That’s a difficult backdrop for any premium newcomer.
Electrek’s Take
I’ve said it before, and I still think it’s true: the TM-B is undeniably cool. Sure, the design is divisive in the classic love-it-or-hate-it way, but the engineer in me nerds out on how cool the technology and design turned out to be. Rivian’s innovative DNA is all over it, and there are some genuinely clever features here.
But I also wonder whether the company has misread where today’s e-bike market is. The industry is still recovering from a painful downturn, consumers have become far more price-conscious, and ALSO has clearly invested heavily in branding, social media marketing, and building out what appears to be a sizable, highly talented workforce that has to be weighing heavily on the company’s burn rate. That’s an expensive way to launch into a market that increasingly rewards value over novelty.
If the riding experience is as polished as ALSO promises, maybe the bike will justify its premium positioning. But after months of delays, the company now has even more to prove. And that has to start with delivering bikes.

title: Trina Solar launches typhoon-resistant PV modules rated up to 8,000 Pa - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
Trina Solar has introduced typhoon-resistant PV modules with mechanical load ratings of up to 8,000 Pa, targeting solar projects in regions exposed to extreme winds.
The new range combines reinforced module frames and glass with self-locking mounting clamps and automated tracker stow strategies designed to improve resilience during severe weather.
Vincent Shaw
13 Aug 2026
Technology & Products
Utility-scale
The new modules installed at Trina’s testing facility | Image: Trina Solar
Trina Solar
has launched a new series of typhoon-resistant PV modules for projects exposed to extreme winds, particularly in coastal China and other typhoon-prone Asian markets.
The Chinese manufacturer said it standard typhoon-resistant module is designed to withstand a rear-side mechanical load of 4,500 Pa, compared with 2,400 Pa for conventional products, adding that the new product is also subjected the design to static loading at 1.05 times its rated level and dynamic loading at 1.5 times the rated level.
At the top of the range is the typhoon-resistant MAX configuration, based on the company’s Vertex N Shield module. Trina lists a static mechanical load capability of over 8,000 Pa, with an optimized frame providing 30% higher downward and 67% higher upward mechanical load capacity.
The company said the load level is designed for conditions associated with China’s Force 17 super-typhoon classification. This designation represents the highest intensity level on the country’s extended wind scale, reserved for the most powerful and destructive tropical cyclones classified as super typhoons.
The design also addresses mounting-system failures. Trina has developed a patented slot-based, self-locking clamp inspired by traditional mortise-and-tenon joints. The clamp mechanically aligns the module and mounting structure and is intended to reduce installation errors and loosening caused by repeated vibration. Trina claims the design can cut installation time by about 25%. The module frame has also been widened by 10% and thickened by 11% to improve load transfer to the supporting structure.
For impact resistance, the MAX version uses reinforced dual glass. Trina’s official product data states that the Vertex N Shield can withstand 75 mm hailstones at a 60-degree tilt. The module has also received IEC 61730 A+A and UL 61730-2 Type 30 (A+A) fire certifications. Trina said earlier RETC testing gave the product “High Achiever” results in thermal cycling, damp heat, static and dynamic mechanical loading, and PID testing.
For tracker-based installations, Trina’s extreme-weather solution combines reinforced modules with its tracking systems and cloud-based wind monitoring. When wind speeds reach preset thresholds, the tracker can automatically move to protective angles, with different strategies applied according to weather conditions.
The focus on wind resilience reflects a growing asset-risk issue for solar developers across eastern and southern China and Southeast Asia. Extreme weather events regularly test energy and other infrastructure across the region. In the past week, Typhoon Dolphin, described by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO) as unusually long-lasting, triggered mass evacuations and severe coastal and inland flood risks, while rainfall records were broken across several Chinese provinces.
IEA PVPS research
identifies structural deformation, cascading mounting failures, airborne debris and flooding among the main threats to PV plants during tropical cyclones. It recommends more robust fastening systems, higher wind-load resistance and improved tracker stow strategies.

title: QBE survey finds DC cabling and plug connections are most common causes of PV fires - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
A survey by global industrial insurer QBE in Great Britain found that the number of fires is rising nearly twice as fast as the number of new photovoltaic installations. After DC cabling and connectors, the most common causes are solar modules, battery storage systems, and inverters.
Jochen Siemer
13 Aug 2026
Research & Development
Cells & modules
Residential
Image: 12019, Pixabay
Industrial insurer QBE has identified a sharp rise in fires linked to photovoltaic systems, based on inquiries made with UK fire services. According to the company, the number of fires increased by 133% between 2022 and 2025. During the same period, the number of installed photovoltaic systems grew by 52%.
Tobias Mehl, risk manager at QBE Germany, views the findings as a significant signal for other markets as well. “Our experience shows that the cause often lies not in the solar modules themselves, but in faulty cable connections, connectors, or other electrical components,” he stated.
According to QBE’s analysis, UK fire services recorded a total of 212 fires linked to photovoltaic systems in 2025, up 133% from 91 fires in 2022. Of the cases recorded in 2025, 49 were attributed to issues with DC cabling and connectors. Solar modules were identified as the cause in 36 cases, battery storage systems in 23 cases, and inverters in 19 cases.
Low overall case numbers
One of these four causes was identified in 127 of the 212 fires. The increasing age of many systems is also considered a significant factor, although QBE did not provide data on the statistical distribution of cases by system age.
Despite the worrying rise, the number of cases remains relatively low compared with the total installed base. According to QBE, around 1.93 million photovoltaic systems were in operation in the UK in 2025. The figure had risen to just over 2 million by June 2026. Consequently, fires caused by photovoltaic components occurred in fewer than 0.07 per 1,000 systems.
Of the 2,025 recorded fires, 102 in 2025 (2024: 87) involved systems in the residential sector, 48 (2024: 33) commercial properties, 14 (2024: 6) industrial properties, and 14 (2024: 16) large-scale solar parks.
The insurer also views the rising number of lithium-ion battery storage systems paired with photovoltaic installations as a cause for “ongoing concern,” noting that firefighting operations in such cases are particularly challenging. According to QBE, the increasing prevalence of battery technology makes it a significant factor in fire statistics overall.
In May, the insurer presented a survey showing that UK fire services had tackled a total of 1,760 fires linked to lithium-ion batteries in 2025. These included 520 involving e-bikes, 279 involving electric cars, and 182 involving e-scooters.

title: Japan’s proposed shading rate for agrivoltaics is unreasonable, says think thank - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
Japan’s Renewable Energy Foundation says proposals to introduce a maximum shading rate of 30% for agrivoltaic installations is contradicted by existing real-world examples where panel shade has helped to cultivate high-quality crops.
Patrick Jowett
13 Aug 2026
Applications & Installations
Research & Development
Highlights
Image: pv magazine / AI generated
Judging crop yield and quality under agrivoltaic systems solely by the shading rates of solar panels is inappropriate, according to new research from the Japan Renewable Energy Foundation (JREF).
The Tokyo-headquartered think tank has
released a report
that analyzes the effects of shading from solar panels on crops including rice, soybeans, tea, coffee, and spinach, using examples from both Japan and internationally.
The research comes ahead of proposals set out by Japan’s Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries to implement new agrivoltaics legislation that would set a uniform shading rate of less than 30%. Public comments on the proposal are being accepted until August 22, ahead of a planned implementation date before the end of September.
JREF argues that the basis for this numerical threshold has not been provided. A statement published on the foundation’s website says that there are many agrivoltaic systems in Japan that are implemented with a shading rate above 30%.
“Even with organic farming that does not use pesticides, sufficient yields and high-quality agricultural products are cultivated and sold under solar panels,” the statement continues. “Such real-world examples contradict the regulation requiring a shading rate of less than 30%. It is not appropriate for the government to implement regulations without scientific basis.”
In the report’s conclusion, JREF calls on the ministry to review the 30% threshold after providing examples of farms that maintain over 80% of their yield with shading rates in excess of 30% thanks to tailored equipment design and cultivation management. It adds that in some cases, high panel shading rates can suppress leaf burn and soil moisture dehydration.
The foundation also highlights that crop yield and quality can be impacted on farms with shading rates less than 30% if the height of the mounting structures or crop cultivation management are not appropriate for the crop.
“Shading rate should be treated as just one condition, and a comprehensive judgment must be made in conjunction with the region, crop, equipment design, and cultivation methods,” the report concludes.
JREF is also advocating for agrivoltaic performance data, covering each region and crop, to be made public so business can utilize and learn from it. The foundation says such data is already held by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, local governments and agricultural committees but is not publicly available or organized in a way that allows for easy reference.
“If it becomes possible to compare data with performance data from similar regions and varieties, the probability of [agrivoltaic] projects succeeding will increase,” the foundation said. “Agricultural committees in municipalities that review temporary land use permits will also be able to more easily assess the suitability of each project.”
JREF also points out that agrivoltaics offer farmers the potential to earn income from electricity generation in addition to agricultural income, in turn helping to stabilize and secure future farming. In the report, the foundation concludes that implementing its recommended measures will help reduce abandoned farmland and idle farmland, leading to the revitalization of Japanese agriculture.
Japan began to establish
tightened standards for agrivoltaics
earlier this year amid reports of reduced crop yields under some existing installations. Updated guidelines gave authorities power to deny approval for projects if crop yields drop by 20% or more, if agricultural activity is neglected, or if panel height and spacing prevent machinery use.
Japan’s cumulative solar capacity likely surpassed 100 GW by the end of last year with
around 5.8 GW
of solar added in 2025.

title: Solar modules with built-in buck converters could raise rooftop PV yield by up to 20% under partial shading - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
TU Delft researchers found that smart PV modules with integrated buck converters can significantly improve energy yields under partial shading by allowing individual substrings to operate independently. The systems delivered 15%-20% more energy than string-inverter systems and 2%-3% more than systems using microinverters or power optimizers, while potentially supporting up to 50% higher module costs at the same LCOE.
Lior Kahana
13 Aug 2026
Research & Development
Residential
Graphical Abstract
| Image: Delft University of Technology, Solar Energy, CC BY 4.0
A research team from
Delft University of Technology
(TU Delft) in the Netherlands has investigated the potential of smart PV modules in urban environments. As simulated in the study, smart PV modules feature built-in buck converters that allow substrings within a module to operate independently, improving energy yield under shaded conditions.
“Although this concept has already been introduced in other studies, the novelty of our work is that we calculate the energy yield of systems with these smart modules under realistic conditions and compare them with conventional systems,” corresponding author Youri Blom told
pv magazine
. “The results show that the smart modules have the highest performance across all considered system topologies.”
Blom said his group plans to further investigate how power electronics can improve the performance of solar panels.
“This is also being applied to four-terminal perovskite-silicon modules. As these devices have two strings, integrated power electronics can play a key role in avoiding the need for additional converters,” he said.
For their research, the team simulated eight PV system configurations using the PVMD Toolbox. The systems combined two TOPCon cell architectures, interdigitated back contact (IBC) and front/back contact (FBC), with four converter topologies.
The reference butterfly modules used 156 mm × 78 mm half-cut cells arranged into six substrings with bypass diodes. The smart modules replaced the bypass diodes with buck converters, allowing each substring to operate independently at its own maximum power point.
The four configurations were butterfly modules with string inverters, butterfly modules with microinverters, butterfly modules with string inverters and power optimizers, and smart modules with string inverters.
The researchers simulated the systems on the same modeled rooftop, using 25 PV modules, in three locations: Rotterdam in the Netherlands, Bogotá in Colombia, and San Francisco in the United States. The rooftop faces southwest at an azimuth of 146 degrees and includes several surrounding objects that create partial shading. The simulations covered a full year.
“The most surprising result was that systems with smart modules can have up to 50% additional module costs and still have the same levelized cost of electricity (LCOE) as the other systems considered,” Blom said. “This means that if the increased cost of power electronics is lower than 50%, the smart modules will have better financial performance. Although it was expected that smart modules would have higher energy yields than conventional systems with microinverters, the fact that they require fewer power converters improves their financial performance.”
The results also showed that the system with smart modules had the highest energy yield among all considered topologies because the substrings can operate independently. This improved shade resilience, resulting in a 15%-20% gain in energy yield compared with the system with string inverters and a 2%-3% gain compared with systems using microinverters or power optimizers.
The novel approach was presented in “
Investigating the energy yield performance of smart photovoltaic modules in shaded environments
,” published in
Solar Energy.

title: Finland adds 478 MW of large-scale solar in H1 - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Finland more than doubled its installed utility-scale solar capacity during the first six months of the year with the commissioning of eight solar plants larger than 1 MW.
Patrick Jowett
13 Aug 2026
Markets & Policy
Highlights
Utility-scale
Image: Oli Heinola/Unsplash
Finland installed 478 MW of utility-scale solar capacity during the first half of 2026 (H1), according to figures from Renewables Finland.
The total more than doubles Finland’s cumulative utility-scale solar capacity, which now stands at 842 MW across 45 operational PV farms larger than 1 MW.
Klaara Tapper, Advocacy Manager at Renewables Finland, told
pv magazine
that eight new solar plants started production in Finland so far this year, including 204 MW Kalanti solar park, which is the country’s largest operational PV site to date.
Total renewables capacity in Finland exceeded 10 GW during H1, with wind power capacity reaching 9,535 MW.
Tapper said European funding has played an important role in completing a number of the recently-commissioned solar parks. Newly-operational projects this year include a 20 MW site in northern Finland that was the
first to be completed
with support from the EU’s cross-border renewables tender scheme.
There have been three rounds of the cross-border tender, with each offering support to large-scale PV projects in Finland. The first round supported
seven Finnish solar projects
, the second round
backed a further seven
, while the third
remains open for applications
until September 1.
“We are enormously glad that these funding mechanisms are available for Finnish solar pv projects,” Tapper said. “The industry has taken huge leaps in terms of growth during the past few years, yet there is still much to learn and a lot to achieve.”
Tapper added that there are small and slow yet positive signs of a national economic upturn in Finland. “As soon as the numerous electricity-hungry industrial investments move forward, so does the demand for renewable energy,” she explained. “Everyone is waiting for the positive signs to turn into actual investment decisions and power purchase agreements.”
In February, Tapper told
pv magazine
new Land Use Act
looks set to bring a new strict zoning requirement that would apply to all solar power plants above 50 hectares. Tapper now added that the new legislation is still forthcoming but is expected to obstruct the prospects of utility-scale solar and has come under criticism from many key players in the green industry field.
Looking ahead, Tapper said the second half of the year is set to be calmer in terms of new utility-scale solar additions to the Finnish grid. “We’re expecting one 100 MW solar park to start electricity production by the end of the year, with a few smaller projects currently under construction, and expected to get ready at some point during 2027,” she explained.
According to figures available on Renewables Finland’s website, there are currently four additional large-scale projects under construction with a combined capacity of 128 MW.
Research from LUT University published earlier this year found Finland has the potential to build out up to
68 GW of PV capacity

title: Scatec completes 1 GW/200 MWh solar-plus-storage project in Egypt - pv magazine Global
content:
Applications & Installations
Scatec has completed Egypt’s 1.1 GW Obelisk solar-plus-storage project, including a 100 MW/200 MWh BESS. The $590 million project will supply Egypt under a 25-year PPA.
Tristan Rayner
13 Aug 2026
Applications & Installations
Batteries
Energy Storage
Utility-scale
Image: Scatec
Norway-based renewable energy developer Scatec has completed Africa’s largest solar-plus-storage project, according to the company, bringing the final 564 MW phase of its Obelisk development online near Nagaa Hammadi, Upper Egypt.
The Obelisk project is a hybrid facility, combining 1.1 GW of solar photovoltaic (PV) capacity, alongside a 100 MW / 200 MWh battery energy storage system (BESS).
Scatec had not responded to a question on the system integrator for the BESS aspect of the project by the time of writing, and typically does not name its partners. BYD Energy said it was Scatec’s partner at its
major Kenhardt project
in South Africa, Scatec’s largest BESS at 225 MW / 1,140 MWh.
The two‑phase build began with a power purchase agreement (PPA) signed in November 2024, with full commercial operations achieved less than two years later.
Scatec said the Obelisk project will deliver over 3,000 GWh of clean electricity annually and will cut emissions by more than 1.2 million tonnes per year, with power generation being supplied to the Egyptian Electricity Transmission Company (EETC) under a 25-year PPA.
“Reaching full commercial operations at Obelisk marks a defining milestone for Scatec. Completing Africa’s largest hybrid solar and battery installation demonstrates our ability to develop, finance, and deliver large-scale renewable energy projects in emerging markets. Obelisk will supply clean, reliable power to Egypt for 25 years and is a tangible contribution to the country’s energy security and transition,” Scatec CEO Terje Pilskog said.
project was financed by a consortium of development finance institutions
, including the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), African Development Bank (AfDB), British International Investment (BII) and European Investment Bank (EIB), which together provided $479 million in senior debt. In total, the Obelisk project costs around $590 million, meaning more than 80% is classified as non-recourse debt.
With Obelisk now online, Scatec has approximately 1.5 GW of solar capacity operational in Egypt, as the new project joins its existing 380 MW BenBan solar plant portfolio. The company is also advancing a pipeline of more than 4.3 GW of renewable energy capacity, as well as 4.1 GWh of BESS in Egypt.
Obelisk contributes to Egypt’s national target of sourcing 42% of its electricity from renewables by 2030, and 60% by 2040.

title: SunEnergyXT launches AC-coupled battery for existing PV systems - pv magazine Global
content:
Technology & Products
SunEnergyXT has launched the SunEnergyXT 500 PRO AC Core, an AC-coupled battery storage system designed for existing PV installations without replacing the inverter. The modular LFP system offers 5 kWh per master unit, scalable to 90 kWh, with smart-home integration, backup power and a 10-year warranty.
Ralph Diermann
13 Aug 2026
Technology & Products
Batteries
Residential
The battery has a capacity of 5 kWh | Image: Sunenergy XT
A photovoltaic system may have been generating electricity for years before its owner decides to add battery storage. To address this market, Chinese company SunEnergyXT has launched an AC-coupled storage system in Germany. The system is installed entirely on the AC side, allowing it to be added without modifying the existing photovoltaic system or replacing the existing inverter, according to the manufacturer.
The SunEnergyXT 500 PRO AC Core comes with hardware for a future direct connection of PV modules. It features four PV inputs, each with 625 W of MPPT power, or three inputs with 800 W each. The inputs are deactivated in the factory software but can be enabled for an additional fee. This allows the system to be expanded without additional hardware or replacing the storage unit.
Each master unit combines a bidirectional inverter with a rated output of 2,400 W, an AC charging capacity of up to 2,400 W, and a 5 kWh lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery. The storage capacity can be expanded modularly to 30 kWh by adding up to five expansion units.
Up to two additional master units can also be connected. Each adds 5 kWh of storage capacity and 2,400 W of input and output power. In the maximum configuration, the system provides 90 kWh of storage capacity and an output of 7.2 kW per phase. This allows installers to match storage capacity and power output to the existing PV system and the customer’s electricity demand. The modular architecture also allows the system to be expanded as demand increases.
SunEnergyXT specifies a service life of at least 10,000 charge-discharge cycles and offers a 10-year manufacturer’s warranty.
Commissioning is carried out through the SunEnergyXT app. After installation, the storage system can be connected to a compatible smart meter, including the Shelly Pro 3EM, Shelly EM-50, Eco-Tracker IR, Eco-Tracker P1 and bitShake models.
The system then provides access to intelligent energy management functions. According to SunEnergyXT, it can also be integrated into smart home platforms such as Home Assistant and operated locally without relying on the cloud.
For backup power, the system has an integrated emergency power outlet rated at 2,400 W. In UPS mode, the changeover from grid-connected to off-grid operation takes a maximum of 10 ms, while standard mode requires less than two seconds.
The enclosure has an IP65 rating and is suitable for outdoor installation. The system operates at temperatures ranging from -20 C to 55 C and uses passive, fanless cooling.
“Many operators of existing photovoltaic systems want to store the electricity they generate themselves without having to modify their existing installation. That is exactly what we developed the AC Core for,” said Chengyuan Zhai, managing director of SunEnergyXT.
